rootbridges.title: LIVING ROOT BRIDGES
scenes: hook
Bridges that grow
In the rainy hills of Meghalaya, in India, there are bridges that are alive.
a stone-colored river gorge in a green rainforest with a thick tangle of tree roots forming a bridge over a stream, misty morning, no people
grow
Guided roots
Villagers guide the roots of rubber fig trees across the river, using bamboo and hollow trunks to hold them.
young tree roots wrapped along a bamboo frame stretching over a jungle stream, close view, no people
slow
Patience
It takes about fifteen years before a bridge is strong enough to walk on.
a calendar-like row of the same root bridge shown growing thicker in several stages, soft jungle light, no people
strong
Stronger with age
And unlike steel, it gets stronger as the roots keep thickening, so some can last for hundreds of years.
a thick old tree root bridge covered with moss over a clear river, sturdy and ancient, no people
long
One of the longest
One of the longest is about fifty three metres across.
a very long root bridge crossing a wide misty valley river, seen from far away, tiny silhouettes of walkers from behind
unesco
World Heritage hopes
Their villages were added to India's tentative list for UNESCO World Heritage in twenty twenty two.
a green village hillside in monsoon rain with a root bridge below, wide scenic view, no people
end
Grown, not built
You don't build this bridge once. You grow it, and the next generation inherits it.
two hands from behind guiding a young green root onto a bamboo frame in the jungle, warm light, no faces

roopkund.title: THE SKELETON LAKE
scenes: hook
A lake of bones
High in the Indian Himalayas, a frozen lake is surrounded by human skeletons.
a small dark lake in a snowy high mountain bowl with scattered pale bones on the shore, cold blue light, no people
where
5,000 metres up
Roopkund Lake sits at about five thousand metres, and its bones were left in the ice and snow.
a vast snowy Himalayan basin with a tiny frozen lake far below tall white peaks, wide view, no people
old
One disaster?
For years, people assumed everyone died together in one disaster, around eight hundred A.D.
a stormy dark sky over a snowy mountain pass with hail falling, dramatic, no people
dna
DNA surprise
In twenty nineteen, scientists studied the DNA of thirty eight of the skeletons, and found they were not one group.
a glowing DNA double helix drawn over an old skull on a lab table, simple shapes, no faces
south
Two eras
Most had South Asian ancestry, but they died at different times, in more than one event.
two rows of simple bone icons on a timeline stretching across a snowy landscape, no faces
med
From far away
Another fourteen had Mediterranean ancestry, and died about a thousand years later.
an old sailing ship on a blue sea next to snowy mountains in the same picture, dreamlike, no people
end
Still unsolved
Why were Mediterranean travellers in the Himalayas? The study could not say.
a lonely trail of footprints in deep snow leading up toward a misty mountain lake, no people

botodolphin.title: THE PINK DOLPHIN
scenes: hook
A pink dolphin
In the Amazon, there is a dolphin that turns pink.
a pink river dolphin breaking the surface of a brown Amazon river, simple shapes, calm morning
born
Born grey
Amazon river dolphins are born grey, and slowly turn pink as they grow.
a small grey baby river dolphin swimming beside a larger pinkish dolphin in brown water
male
Pinker males
Males tend to be pinker than females, and scientists link this to scars from fights.
two pink river dolphins facing each other in murky water, bubbles, gentle mood
neck
Flexible neck
Their neck bones are not fused like most dolphins, so they can bend and turn their heads easily.
a pink river dolphin bending its long snout and neck sideways between underwater roots
flood
Swimming in forest
When the rains flood the forest, they swim between the trees.
a pink dolphin swimming among tall tree trunks in flooded green rainforest, light rays under water
size
Biggest river dolphin
It is the largest river dolphin species in the world.
a large pink dolphin next to a small wooden canoe seen from above on a wide brown river, no people
end
Under pressure
But fishing and pollution put them at risk, and scientists are still working out how many remain.
an empty fishing net floating in a river at sunset with a dolphin fin far away, solemn

lencois.title: THE DESERT THAT FLOODS
scenes: hook
Desert or not?
This looks like a desert in Brazil. But it gets far more rain than a real desert.
endless white sand dunes under a dramatic sky with turquoise pools between them, wide view, no people
dunes
Giant dunes
Lençóis Maranhenses has endless white dunes, some about forty metres high.
tall smooth white sand dunes with sharp wind-carved ridges, soft golden light, no people
lagoons
Blue lagoons
Between January and June, rain fills the valleys between the dunes, and thousands of blue lagoons appear.
many turquoise lagoons scattered between white dunes seen from above, bright and clear
why
Why they stay
A layer of hard, waterproof sediment under the sand stops the water from draining away.
a cutaway view of white dune sand over a dark flat waterproof layer holding a blue lagoon, simple diagram style
fish
Life returns
Fish arrive with the water, and some survive the dry season by sleeping in the mud.
a small silvery fish in a clear lagoon next to a cracked dry mud patch, close view
unesco
World Heritage
In twenty twenty four, the park became a UNESCO World Heritage site.
a calm lagoon at sunset reflecting orange sky between pale dunes, peaceful, no people
end
Would you swim?
A desert that floods. Would you swim in it?
a single wooden boat floating on a turquoise lagoon surrounded by dunes, from far away, no faces

krakatoa.title: KRAKATOA 1883
scenes: hook
The loudest sound
In eighteen eighty three, a volcano in Indonesia made the loudest sound in modern history.
a huge volcanic explosion over a tropical island with a giant ash column, dramatic orange sky, simple shapes
sound
Heard around the world
People heard it nearly five thousand kilometres away, and its pressure wave circled the Earth more than three times.
concentric sound waves spreading across a globe from a small island, stylized map picture
waves
Giant waves
Huge tsunamis struck the nearby coasts, and over thirty thousand people died, mostly from the waves.
a giant dark wave rising over a small coastal village seen from far away, no people
sky
Red sunsets
Ash and gas in the upper air painted vivid red sunsets around the world for months.
a dramatic deep red and purple sunset sky over a quiet harbor with old ships, no people
cool
A cooler world
Global temperatures dipped, and took about five years to return to normal.
a thermometer drawn over a snowy landscape beside a pale sun, simple shapes
child
Anak Krakatau
Today, a new volcano called Anak Krakatau, the Child of Krakatoa, rises where it once stood.
a small new volcanic cone rising from the sea at dawn with a thin smoke trail, calm mood
end
Still active
A reminder that the ground beneath the sea is still alive.
a calm sea with a tiny volcano silhouette on the horizon under a starry sky, peaceful, no people

kawahijen.title: THE BLUE FIRE
scenes: hook
Blue fire
Deep inside a volcano in Indonesia, a river of fire glows electric blue.
a dark volcano crater at night with glowing electric blue flames and streams, dramatic, no people
not
Not lava
It is not lava. It is sulfur gas, burning when it meets the air.
a yellow sulfur crust and small vents with blue flames flickering at night, close view, no people
flow
Burning rivers
Some of the sulfur condenses into liquid, which burns and flows like blue lava.
blue glowing liquid streams running down a rocky slope in the dark, stylized
lake
Acid lake
Next to it lies a turquoise crater lake, one of the most acidic in the world.
a bright turquoise crater lake with white steam drifting over it at dawn, wide view, no people
miners
Sulfur miners
Miners climb down into the crater, often at night, to collect the yellow sulfur.
a silhouette of a worker with a basket seen from behind climbing steps in a smoky yellow crater at dawn, no face
risk
Harsh fumes
The fumes are hard on the lungs, and the work is dangerous.
thick white and yellow gas clouds filling a crater, a tiny figure from behind far away, solemn mood
end
Beauty and labour
Beauty and hard labour, side by side, inside one crater.
blue flames glowing at the bottom of a dark crater under a starry sky, peaceful and serious, no people

naica.title: THE CAVE OF CRYSTALS
scenes: hook
Giant crystals
Nearly three hundred metres under a Mexican desert, there is a cave of giant crystals.
a cave filled with huge white crystal beams criss-crossing, warm lamp glow, no people
size
Over 11 metres
Some of the crystals are over eleven metres long, among the largest natural crystals ever found.
a huge white crystal beam compared with a tiny human silhouette from behind, no face
what
Selenite
They are selenite, a form of gypsum, grown slowly in hot, mineral rich water.
white crystal beams growing under glowing hot blue water, cutaway cave, simple shapes
heat
Deadly heat
But the air is about fifty eight degrees Celsius, and extremely humid.
hot orange steam in a crystal cave with a red thermometer symbol, no people
suit
Cooling suits
Without special cooling gear, a person can survive there only a short time.
a researcher in a bulky silver cooling suit seen from behind in a crystal cave, no face
flood
Flooding again
The mine closed in twenty fifteen because of flooding, and the cave is hard to reach today.
dark water slowly rising around white crystals in a cave, quiet mood, no people
end
Sealed again
A hidden world, grown in the dark, and sealed away again.
a glowing white crystal beam half under dark still water, mysterious, no people

axolotl.title: THE AXOLOTL
scenes: hook
Smiling regrower
This smiling animal can grow back its own limbs.
a cute pink axolotl with feathery gills smiling in clear water, centered, simple shapes
where
Only in Xochimilco
It is the axolotl, and in the wild it lives only around Xochimilco, near Mexico City.
colorful flat boats on green canals with floating gardens in Mexico City, a tiny axolotl in the water, no people
baby
Never grows up
Unlike most salamanders, it keeps its baby features, like feathery gills, for life.
an axolotl with big feathery gills next to a small land salamander for comparison, simple picture
regrow
Regrowing
It can regrow limbs, organs, and even parts of its brain.
an axolotl with a new small front leg growing back beside a drawn dotted outline of the old leg
science
Why scientists care
That is why scientists study them, hoping to learn more about healing.
a microscope and a glass tank with an axolotl on a lab table, warm light, no people
wild
Critically endangered
In the wild, they are critically endangered, with fewer than a thousand estimated to remain.
a lonely axolotl in murky green canal water with a few empty lily pads, solemn
end
Help needed
Polluted canals and invasive fish hurt them. Thousands live in tanks, but wild ones need help.
a clean clear canal with water plants and a small axolotl hiding among them, hopeful light, no people
